106/**
107 * SsTable provides a way to display information from a database in a table
108 * format (aka "spreadsheet" or "datasheet" view). The SsTable takes a
109 * RowSet as a source of data. It also provides different cell renderers
110 * including a comboboxes renderer and a date renderer.
111 * <p>
112 * SsTable internally uses the SsTableModel to display the information in a
113 * table format. SsTable also provides an easy means for displaying headers.
114 * Columns can be hidden or made uneditable. In addition, it provides much finer
115 * control over which cells can be edited and which cells can't be edited. It
116 * uses the SsCellEditing interface for achieving this. The implementation of
117 * this interface also provides a way to specify what kind of information is
118 * valid for each cell.
119 * <p>
120 * SsTable maps Control-X to delete multiple selected rows.
121 * Adds copy/paste handling of rectangular regions.
122 * <p>
123 * SsTable uses the isCellEditable() method in SsCellEditing to determine if
124 * a cell is editable or not. The cellUpdateRequested() method of SsCellEditing
125 * is used to notify a user program when an update is requested. While doing so
126 * it provides the present value in the cell and also the new value. Based on
127 * this information the new value can be rejected or accepted by the program.
128 * <p>
129 * SsTable also provides an "extra" row to facilitate the addition of rows to
130 * the table. Default values for various columns can be set programmatically. A
131 * programmer can also specify which column is the primary key column for the
132 * underlying RowSet and supply a primary key for that column when a new row
133 * is being added.
134 * <p>
135 * While using the headers always set them before you set the RowSet.
136 * Otherwise the headers will not appear.
137 * <p>
138 * Also if you are using column names rather than column numbers for different
139 * function you have to call them only after setting the RowSet. Because
140 * SsTable uses the RowSet to convert the column names to column numbers.
141 * If you specify the column numbers you can do before or after setting the
142 * RowSet, it does not matter.
143 * <p>
144 * You can simply remember this order
145 * <ol>
146 * <li>Set the headers
147 * <li>Set the RowSet
148 * <li>Any other function calls.
149 * </ol>
150 * <b>Simple Example</b>:
151 * {@snippet class=DataGridSnippets region=init1}
152 *
153 * Also See Examples 5, 6, 7 in the samples.
154 */
155@SuppressWarnings("serial")
156public class SsTable extends JTable {
157  // TODO BUG? there's no programatic way to change COPY/PASTE.

159  // TODO Add documentation for CUT/PASTE keys/operation.

167  /**
168   * Editor for check box fields.
169   */
170  protected class CheckBoxEditor extends DefaultCellEditor {
171    /** Variable to store the sql type. */
172    protected JDBCType columnClass = null;
173
174    /** Grid boolean editor. */
175    public CheckBoxEditor() {
176      super(new JCheckBox());
177    }
178
179    /** @return boolean/int */
180    @Override
181    public Object getCellEditorValue() {
182      // GET THE COMPONENT AND CHECK IF IT IS CHECKED OR NOT.
183      boolean isSelected = ((JCheckBox) getComponent()).isSelected();
184
185      // CHECK THE COLUMN TYPE AND RETURN CORRESPONDING OBJECT.
186      // IF IT IS INTEGER THEN 1 IS CONSIDERED TRUE AND 0 FALSE.
187      if (columnClass == JDBCType.BOOLEAN) {
188        return isSelected;
189      } else {
190        return isSelected ? 1 : 0;
191      }
192    }
193
194    /** {@inheritDoc} */
195    @Override
196    public Component getTableCellEditorComponent(JTable table, Object value, boolean selected,
197                                                 int row, int column) {
198      // GET THE COMPONENT RENDERING THE VALUE.
199      final JCheckBox checkBox = (JCheckBox) getComponent();
200      boolean isSelected = false;
201
202      // CHECK THE TYPE OF COLUMN, IT SHOULD BE THE SAME AS THE TYPE OF VALUE.
203      switch (value) {
204        case Boolean b -> {
205          columnClass = JDBCType.BOOLEAN; // STORE THE TYPE OF COLUMN WE NEED
206          isSelected = b;
207        }
208        case Integer i -> {
209          columnClass = JDBCType.INTEGER; // STORE THE COLUMN CLASS.
210          // A VALUE OF 0 IS FALSE - ANY OTHER VALUE IS TRUE
211          isSelected = i != 0;
212        }
213        default -> // THE COLUMN IS NOT BOOLEAN OR INTEGER, LOG ERROR MESSAGE.
214          logger.log(Level.ERROR, "Can't set check box value. Unknown data type. Column type "
215                                      + "should be Boolean or Integer for check box columns.");
216      }
217
218      checkBox.setSelected(isSelected); // USE VALUE TO CHECK OR UNCHECK BOX.
219      return checkBox;
220    }
221  }
222
223  /**
224   * Renderer for check box fields.
225   */
226  protected class CheckBoxRenderer extends JCheckBox implements TableCellRenderer {
227    /** {@inheritDoc} */
228    @Override
229    public Component getTableCellRendererComponent(JTable table, Object value, boolean selected,
230                                                   boolean hasFocus, int row, int column) {
231      boolean isSelected = false;
232      switch (value) {
233        case Boolean b -> isSelected = b;
234        case Integer i -> isSelected = i != 0;
235        default ->
236          logger.log(Level.ERROR, "Can't set check box value. Unknown data type. Column type "
237                                      + "should be Boolean or Integer for check box columns.");
238      }
239      setSelected(isSelected);
240
241      return this;
242    }
243  }

245  /**
246   * Editor for combo box fields.
247   */
248  protected class ComboEditor extends DefaultCellEditor {
249    // Set the # of clicks required to edit the combo to 2.
250    final int tmpClickCountToStart = 2;
251    final Object[] items;
252    final Object[] underlyingValues;
253
254    /**
255     * Combo Editor.
256     * @param items the combo items
257     * @param underlyingValues database values; may be null
258     */
259    public ComboEditor(Object[] items, Object[] underlyingValues) {
260      super(new GridComboEditorComboBox());
261      // TODO: copy the arrays? Or just agree that they are never modified.
262      //         Could use guava immutable then not worry about it.
263      this.items = Arrays.copyOf(items, items.length);
264      this.underlyingValues = Arrays.copyOf(underlyingValues, underlyingValues.length);
265
266      getComponent().setModel(new GridComboModels().getComboModel());
267    }
268
269    /** {@inheritDoc} */
270    @Override
271    @SuppressWarnings("NonPublicExported")
272    final public GridComboEditorComboBox getComponent() {
273      return (GridComboEditorComboBox) super.getComponent();
274    }
275
276    /**
277     * Combo editor value.
278     * @return value for selected item
279     */
280    @Override
281    public Object getCellEditorValue() {
282      final GridComboModels.GridComboItem item = getComponent().getGridSelItem();
283
284      if (item == null) {
285        return underlyingValues != null ? underlyingValues[0] : null;
286      }
287
288      logger.log(TRACE, () -> sf("Item %s:%s", item.getElem(0), item.getElem(1)));
289      return item.getElem(1);
290    }
291
292    /**
293     * Return index of value in underlyingValues.
294     * @param value look for this
295     * @return index or -1 if can not find
296     */
297    protected int getIndexOf(Object value) {
298      if (underlyingValues == null) {
299        // IF THE VALUE IS NULL THEN SET THE DISPLAY ON THE COMBO TO BLANK (INDEX -1)
300        if (value == null) {
301          return -1;
302        }
303        return ((Integer) value);
304      }
305      for (int i = 0; i < underlyingValues.length; i++) {
306        if (underlyingValues[i].equals(value)) {
307          return i;
308        }
309      }
310
311      return -1;
312    }
313
314    /** {@inheritDoc} */
315    @Override
316    public Component getTableCellEditorComponent(JTable table, Object value, boolean selected,
317                                                 int row, int column) {
318      final JComboBox<?> comboBox = getComponent();
319      comboBox.setSelectedIndex(getIndexOf(value));
320      return comboBox;
321    }
322
323    /** {@inheritDoc} */
324    @Override
325    public boolean isCellEditable(EventObject event) {
326      if (event instanceof MouseEvent mouseEvent) {
327        return mouseEvent.getClickCount() >= tmpClickCountToStart;
328      }
329      return true;
330    }
331
332    /**
333     * Simple combox model that maps each combobox item to
334     * the index into this ComboEditor's items array.
335     */
336    private final class GridComboModels extends SimpleComboListSwingModel {
337      private GridComboModels() {
338        super(2, new ArrayList<>(items.length));
339        try (Remodel remodel = getRemodel()) {
340          for (int i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {
341            remodel.add(new GridComboItem(i));
342          }
343        }
344      }
345
346      @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
347      @Override
348      public ComboBoxModel<GridComboItem> getComboModel() {
349        return (ComboBoxModel<GridComboItem>) super.getComboModel();
350      }
351
352      class GridComboItem implements ListItem0, Cloneable {
353        private final int listIdx;
354
355        public GridComboItem(int listIdx) {
356          this.listIdx = listIdx;
357        }
358
359        @Override
360        public Object getElem(int index) {
361          return index == 0          ? items[listIdx]
362          : underlyingValues != null ? underlyingValues[listIdx]
363                                     : listIdx;
364        }
365        @Override
366        public Object clone() throws CloneNotSupportedException {
367          return super.clone();
368        }
369        @Override
370        public String toString() {
371          return items[listIdx].toString();
372        }
373      }
374    }
375  }
376
377  private final class GridComboEditorComboBox
378      extends JComboBox<ComboEditor.GridComboModels.GridComboItem> {
379    public ComboEditor.GridComboModels.GridComboItem getGridSelItem() {
380      return (ComboEditor.GridComboModels.GridComboItem) super.getSelectedItem();
381    }
382  }

384  /**
385   * Renderer for combo box fields.
386   */
387  protected class ComboRenderer extends DefaultTableCellRenderer.UIResource {
388    Object[] displayValues = null;
389    Object[] underlyingValues = null;
390
391    /**
392     * Combo renderer.
393     * @param items the combo items
394     * @param underlyingValues database values; may be null
395     */
396    public ComboRenderer(Object[] items, Object[] underlyingValues) {
397      this.underlyingValues = underlyingValues;
398      this.displayValues = items;
399    }
400
401    /**
402     * Return index of value in underlyingValues.
403     * return index of first item if match not found.
404     * @param value look for this
405     * @return index
406     */
407    protected int getIndexOf(Object value) {
408      if (value == null) {
409        return -1;
410      }
411      if (underlyingValues == null) {
412        return ((Integer) value);
413      }
414      for (int i = 0; i < underlyingValues.length; i++) {
415        if (underlyingValues[i].equals(value)) {
416          return i;
417        }
418      }
419      return 0;
420    }
421
422    /** {@inheritDoc} */
423    @Override
424    public Component getTableCellRendererComponent(JTable table, Object value, boolean selected,
425                                                   boolean hasFocus, int row, int column) {
426      final JLabel label = (JLabel) super.getTableCellRendererComponent(table, value, selected,
427                                                                        hasFocus, row, column);
428
429      int index = -1;
430      if (displayValues.length > 0) {
431        index = getIndexOf(value);
432      } else {
433        logger.log(Level.ERROR, () -> "No item in combo that corresponds to " + value);
434      }
435
436      if (index == -1) {
437        label.setText("");
438      } else {
439        label.setText(displayValues[index].toString());
440      }
441      return label;
442    }
443  }

445  // https://forums.oracle.com/ords/apexds/post/date-editing-in-a-jtable-1380
446  private class DateEditor extends DefaultCellEditor {
447    int cIdx;
448    private DateEditor(int cIdx) {
449      super(new JTextField());
450      this.cIdx = cIdx;
451    }
452
453    @Override
454    public Object getCellEditorValue() {
455      String strDate = ((JTextField) getComponent()).getText();
456      return (Date) getSQLDateTimeObject(strDate, RSC.get(rowsModel, cIdx + 1));
457    }
458
459    @Override
460    public Component getTableCellEditorComponent(JTable table, Object value, boolean isSelected,
461                                                 int row, int column) {
462      JTextField tf = ((JTextField) getComponent());
463      tf.setBorder(new LineBorder(Color.black));
464      try {
465        tf.setText(getDateTimeText(value, RSC.get(rowsModel, cIdx + 1)));
466      } catch (Exception e) {
467        tf.setText("");
468      }
469      return tf;
470    }
471
472    public boolean parseDate(String value) {
473      Object dto = getSQLDateTimeObject(value, RSC.get(rowsModel, cIdx + 1));
474      return dto != null;
475    }
476
477    @Override
478    public boolean stopCellEditing() {
479      String value = ((JTextField) getComponent()).getText();
480      if (!value.isEmpty()) {
481        if (!parseDate(value)) {
482          ((JComponent) getComponent()).setBorder(new LineBorder(Color.red));
483          return false;
484        }
485      }
486      return super.stopCellEditing();
487    }
488  } // end DateEditor

585  /**
586   * Renderer for date fields. Displays dates using mm/dd/yyyy format.
587   */
588  protected class DateRenderer extends DefaultTableCellRenderer {
589    private final int cIdx;
590
591    private DateRenderer(int cIdx) {
592      this.cIdx = cIdx;
593    }
594
595    /**
596     * Set the value to render. Expect date; if not, give it to super.
597     * @param value probably a date
598     */
599    @Override
600    public void setValue(Object value) {
601      if (value instanceof java.sql.Date date) {
602        String strDate = getDateTimeText(date, RSC.get(rowsModel, cIdx + 1));
603        setHorizontalAlignment(SwingConstants.CENTER);
604        setText(strDate);
605      } else {
606        super.setValue(value);
607      }
608    }
609  }

611  /**
612   * This is the default editor for Numeric, String and Object column types.
613   */
614  class DefaultEditor extends DefaultCellEditor {
615    /**
616     * Implementation of KeyListener and FocusListener for the editor component.
617     */
618    protected class MyListener implements KeyListener, FocusListener {
619      int keyPressed = 0;
620
621      /**
622       * Select all text when focus is gained
623       */
624      @Override
625      public void focusGained(FocusEvent fe) {
626        ((JTextField) getComponent()).selectAll();
627      }
628
629      /**
630       * sets the keyPressed variable to zero.
631       */
632      @Override
633      public void focusLost(FocusEvent fe) {
634        // Set the key press tracker to 0 when the field loses focus.
635        keyPressed = 0;
636      }
637
638      /**
639       * Increment the key pressed variable when ever there is a key pressed event, other than the Tab key.
640       * <p>
641       * It is assumed that the editor will not get the keyPressed event for the first key,
642       * which triggers the editor. That event is consumed by the JTable.
643       */
644      @Override
645      public void keyPressed(KeyEvent ke) {
646        if (ke.getKeyCode() != KeyEvent.VK_TAB) {
647          keyPressed++;
648        }
649      }
650
651      /**
652       * Based on if this is first key release event the contents will be cleared
653       */
654      @Override
655      public void keyReleased(KeyEvent ke) {
656        final JComponent editor = (JComponent) DefaultEditor.this.getComponent();
657        if (editor instanceof JTextField jtf) {
658          if ((keyPressed == 0) && Character.isLetterOrDigit(ke.getKeyChar())) {
659            jtf.setText(String.valueOf(ke.getKeyChar()));
660          }
661        }
662        keyPressed--;
663        if (keyPressed < 0) {
664          keyPressed = 0;
665        }
666      }
667
668      @Override
669      public void keyTyped(KeyEvent ke) {
670        // do nothing
671      }
672    }
673
674    /**
675     * Constructor to instantiate an object of column type from a string.
676     */
677    Constructor<?> constructor;
678
679    /**
680     * Value of the editor.
681     */
682    // TODO: get rid of value, see getCellEditorValue/stopCellEditing
683    //       We could probably create a new method getCellValue and use
684    //       initial part of stopCellEditing code in it and then call
685    //       this new funds getCellEditorValue and in stopCellEditing.
686    Object value;

688    /**
689     * Constructs Default Editor.
690     */
691    public DefaultEditor() {
692      super(new SsTextField()); // TODO: just JTextField
693      getComponent().setFocusTraversalKeysEnabled(false);
694      final MyListener listener = new MyListener();
695      getComponent().addFocusListener(listener);
696      getComponent().addKeyListener(listener);
697    }

699    /**
700     * Returns the cell value.
701     */
702    @Override
703    public Object getCellEditorValue() {
704      return value;
705    }
706
707    @Override
708    @SuppressWarnings({"UseSpecificCatch", "BroadCatchBlock", "TooBroadCatch"})
709    public Component getTableCellEditorComponent(JTable table, Object value, boolean isSelected,
710                                                 int row, int column) {
711      // SET INITIAL VALUE TO NULL.
712      this.value = null;
713
714      ((JComponent) getComponent()).setBorder(new LineBorder(Color.black));
715
716      // GET A CONSTRUCTOR FOR AN OBJECT OF THE CURRENT COLUMN TYPE.
717      // THIS IS NEEDED FOR RETURNING THE VALUE IN COLUMN CLASS OBJECT
718      try {
719        Class<?> type = table.getColumnClass(column);
720        if (type == Object.class) {
721          type = String.class;
722        }
723        constructor = type.getConstructor(new Class<?>[] {String.class});
724      } catch (final Exception e) {
725        return null;
726      }
727
728      return super.getTableCellEditorComponent(table, value, isSelected, row, column);
729    }
730
731    @Override
732    @SuppressWarnings({"UseSpecificCatch", "TooBroadCatch"})
733    public boolean stopCellEditing() {
734      final String s = (String) super.getCellEditorValue();
735
736      if (s.trim().isEmpty()) {
737        if (constructor.getDeclaringClass() == String.class) {
738          value = s;
739        }
740      } else {
741        try {
742          value = constructor.newInstance(new Object[] {s});
743        } catch (final Exception e) {
744          // DRAW A RED BORDER IF THE VALUE OBJECT CAN'T BE CREATED.
745          // PROBABLY THE DATA ENTERED IS NOT RIGHT (STRING IN NUMBER FIELD OR VICE-VERSA)
746          ((JComponent) getComponent()).setBorder(new LineBorder(Color.red));
747          return false;
748        }
749      }
750
751      return super.stopCellEditing();
752    }
753  }

892  private class Sorter extends TableRowSorter<SsTableModel> {
893    public Sorter(SsTableModel model) {
894      super(model);
895    }
896
897    /** Cycle: {@literal ASC --> DESC --> UNSORTED --> ASC} ... */
898    @Override
899    public void toggleSortOrder(int column) {
900      List<SortKey> keys = new ArrayList<>(getSortKeys());
901      // The primary sorting key may get some special handling
902      if (!keys.isEmpty() && keys.get(0).getColumn() == column) {
903        if (keys.get(0).getSortOrder() == SortOrder.DESCENDING) {
904          // cycle from descending no sort on primary key
905          if (REMOVE_KEYS_IF_PRIMARY_UNSORTED) {
906            // Like removing all keys.
907            // Next toggle restores sorts.
908            keys.set(0, new SortKey(column, SortOrder.UNSORTED));
909          } else {
910            // Remove the primary key, any remaining keys will sort.
911            // Like backing out key by key.
912            keys.remove(0);
913          }
914          setSortKeys(keys);
915          return;
916        }
917      }
918      super.toggleSortOrder(column);
919    }
920  }
921
922  /** Note: toggling insertion on/off/on/off does not create new sorter. */
923  // TODO: both setInsertion/setSorting toggle; is that the right thing?
924  private void checkCreateAddSorter(boolean clearFirst) {
925    logger.log(
926        DEBUG,
927        () -> sf("clear: %b, sorting %b, insert %b", clearFirst, getSorting(), getInsertion()));
928    if (clearFirst || !getSorting()) {
929      RowSorter<?> rowSorter = getRowSorter();
930
931      if (rowSorter != null) // clear column sorted indicators
932        rowSorter.setSortKeys(null);
933      setRowSorter(null);
934      savedRowSorterKeys = null;
935      savedRowFilter = null;
936    }
937    if (!getSorting())
938      return;
939
940    // sorting's enabled, save or restore state as needed
941
942    if (getInsertion()) { // save rowSorter state: keys, filter
943      RowSorter<?> rowSorter = getRowSorter();
944      if (rowSorter == null) {
945        savedRowSorterKeys = null; // to be sure
946        savedRowFilter = null;
947        return;
948      }
949      // make sure the types are OK
950      if (!(rowSorter instanceof Sorter) || !(rowSorter.getModel() instanceof SsTableModel)) {
951        logger.log(Level.ERROR, () -> "Wrong sorter type: " + rowSorter);
952        return;
953      }
954      // cast to correct types
955      Sorter sorter = (Sorter) rowSorter;
956      @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
957      RowFilter<SsTableModel, Integer> t = (RowFilter<SsTableModel, Integer>) sorter.getRowFilter();
958      // and save the state
959      savedRowFilter = t;
960      savedRowSorterKeys = sorter.getSortKeys();
961      // and clear current
962      sorter.setSortKeys(null);
963      sorter.setRowFilter(null);
964      setRowSorter(null);
965    } else { // restore sorting/filtering
966      Sorter rowSorter = new Sorter(getModel());
967      setRowSorter(rowSorter);
968      rowSorter.setSortKeys(savedRowSorterKeys);
969      rowSorter.setRowFilter(savedRowFilter);
970    }
971  }

973  /**
974   * Initializes the data grid control. Collects metadata information about the
975   * given RowSet.
976   */
977  // TODO: does this need to be overridable? It's called from constructor.
978  protected final void bind() {
979    try {
980      // EXECUTE THE QUERY
981      if (callExecute) {
982        rowSet.execute();
983      }
984
985      // SPECIFY THE SSROWSET TO THE TABLE MODEL.
986      getModel().setRowsModel(rowsModel);
987
988    } catch (final SQLException se) {
989      logger.log(Level.ERROR, "SQL Exception.", se);
990    }
991
992    // THIS IS NEEDED IF THE NUMBER OF COLUMNS IN THE NEW SSROWSET
993    // DOES NOT MATCH WITH THE OLD COLUMNS.
994    createDefaultColumnModel();
995
996    // HIDE COLUMNS AS NEEDED
997    hideColumns();
998  } // end protected void bind() {

1114  /**
1115   * Returns the list of selected, visible columns. This function gets the list of selected
1116   * columns from parent class and removes any columns which are present in hidden
1117   * columns.
1118   * <p>
1119   * This was needed because when doing a copy/paste operation, hidden columns were included
1120   * with the initial selection.
1121   *
1122   * @return array of selected columns
1123   */
1124  @Override
1125  public int[] getSelectedColumns() {
1126    // IF THERE ARE NO HIDDEN COLUMNS THEN RETURN THE SAME LIST
1127    if (hiddenColumnsList.isEmpty()) {
1128      return super.getSelectedColumns();
1129    }
1130
1131    return IntStream.of(super.getSelectedColumns())
1132        .filter((selCol) -> !hiddenColumnsList.contains(selCol))
1133        .toArray();
1134  }

1163  /**
1164   * Hides the columns specified in the hidden columns list.
1165   */
1166  protected void hideColumns() {
1167    // Set width of hidden columns to 0
1168    // TODO: maybe remove the column instead, with ability to restore.
1169
1170    for (TableColumn col : getColumnsList()) {
1171      if (hiddenColumnsList.contains(col.getModelIndex())) {
1172        // Set hidden column width to 0
1173        col.setMinWidth(0);
1174        col.setMaxWidth(0);
1175        col.setPreferredWidth(0);
1176      } else {
1177        // TODO: Does this belong in init()?
1178        if (getAutoResizeMode() == AUTO_RESIZE_OFF) {
1179          col.setPreferredWidth(columnWidth);
1180        }
1181        // Restore the column to some visibility
1182        if (col.getMinWidth() == 0 && col.getMaxWidth() <= 15) {
1183          // If the column used to be hidden, then restore it to defaults
1184          // TODO: not sure where the 15 comes from, but ...
1185          col.setMaxWidth(Integer.MAX_VALUE);
1186          col.setPreferredWidth(columnWidth);
1187          col.setMinWidth(15);
1188        }
1189      }
1190    }
1191  }

1193  /**
1194   * Initialization code.
1195   */
1196  protected final void init() {
1197    // FORCE JTABLE TO SURRENDER TO THE EDITOR WHEN KEYSTROKES CAUSE THE EDITOR TO
1198    // BE ACTIVATED
1199    setSurrendersFocusOnKeystroke(true);
1200    setDefaultEditor(Number.class, new DefaultEditor());
1201    setDefaultEditor(String.class, new DefaultEditor());
1202    setDefaultEditor(Object.class, new DefaultEditor());
1203
1204    // Handle Control-X for selected rows deletion
1205    KeyStroke ks = KeyStroke.getKeyStroke("control released X");
1206    String key = "GridDeleteSelectedRows";
1207    getInputMap(WHEN_FOCUSED).put(ks, key);
1208    getActionMap().put(key, new AbstractAction() {
1209      @Override
1210      public void actionPerformed(ActionEvent e) {
1211        if (!allowDeletion)
1212          return;
1213        final int numRows = getSelectedRowCount();
1214        if (numRows == 0) {
1215          return;
1216        }
1217        final int[] rows = getSelectedRows();
1218        // CONFIRM THE DELETION
1219        final int returnValue = JOptionPane.showConfirmDialog(
1220            messageWindow, "You are about to delete " + rows.length + " rows. "
1221                               + "\nAre you sure you want to delete the rows?");
1222        if (returnValue != JOptionPane.YES_OPTION) {
1223          return;
1224        }
1225        // Convert visual row numbers to model row numbers
1226        for (int i = 0; i < rows.length; ++i) {
1227          rows[i] = convertRowIndexToModel(rows[i]);
1228        }
1229        Arrays.sort(rows);
1230        // Delete in reverse order so row numbers don't change while deleting
1231        for (int i = rows.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
1232          getModel().deleteRow(rows[i]);
1233        }
1234      }
1235    });
1236
1237    // CREATE AN INSTANCE OF KEY ADAPTER ADD PROVIDE THE PRESET GRID TO THE ADAPTER.
1238    // THIS IS FOR COPY AND PASTE SUPPORT
1239    final SsTableKeyAdapter keyAdapter = new SsTableKeyAdapter(this);
1240    keyAdapter.setAllowInsertion(true);
1241
1242    // SPECIFY THE MESSAGE WINDOW TO WHICH THE TABLE MODEL HAS TO POP UP
1243    // ERROR MESSAGES.
1244    getModel().setMessageWindow(messageWindow);
1245
1246    // THIS CAUSES THE JTABLE TO DISPLAY THE HORIZONTAL SCROLL BAR AS NEEDED.
1247    // CODE IN HIDECOLUMNS FUNCTION DEPENDS ON THIS VARIABLE.
1248    setAutoResizeMode(JTable.AUTO_RESIZE_OFF);
1249
1250    // ADD THE JTABLE TO A SCROLL BAR
1251    scrollPane = new JScrollPane(this, ScrollPaneConstants.VERTICAL_SCROLLBAR_AS_NEEDED,
1252                                 ScrollPaneConstants.HORIZONTAL_SCROLLBAR_AS_NEEDED);
1253
1254  } // end protected void init() {

1498  /**
1499   * Sets the column numbers that should be hidden. The SsTable sets the column
1500   * width of these columns to 0. The columns are set to zero width rather than
1501   * removing the column from the table. Thus preserving the column numbering. If a
1502   * column is removed then the column numbers for columns after the removed
1503   * column will change. Make sure that you specify the hidden column numbers in
1504   * the uneditable column list.
1505   * <p>
1506   * Currently not a bean property since there is no associated variable.
1507   *
1508   * @param columnNumbers array specifying the column numbers which should be
1509   *                       hidden
1510   */
1511  public void setHiddenColumns(List<Integer> columnNumbers) {
1512    Objects.requireNonNull(columnNumbers);
1513
1514    hiddenColumnsList = new ArrayList<>(columnNumbers);
1515    hideColumns();
1516  }

1518  /**
1519   * Sets the columns, by name, that should be hidden. The SsTable sets the column
1520   * width of these columns to 0. The columns are set to zero width rather than
1521   * removing the column from the table. Thus preserving the column numbering. If a
1522   * column is removed then the column numbers for columns after the removed
1523   * column will change. Make sure that you specify the hidden column numbers in
1524   * the uneditable column list.
1525   * <p>
1526   * Currently not a bean property since there is no associated variable.
1527   *
1528   * @param columnNames array specifying the column names which should be hidden
1529   * @throws SQLException   SQLException
1530   */
1531  public void setHiddenColumnsByName(List<String> columnNames) throws SQLException {
1532    Objects.requireNonNull(columnNames);
1533    List<Integer> hiddenCols = new ArrayList<>(columnNames.size());
1534    for (String colName : columnNames) {
1535      hiddenCols.add(RowSetOps.getColumnIndex(rowSet, colName) - 1);
1536    }
1537    setHiddenColumns(hiddenCols);
1538  }

1551  /**
1552   * Sets the allowInsertion property of the table. If set to true an additional
1553   * row for inserting new rows will be displayed
1554   *
1555   * @param insertion true if new rows can be added else false.
1556   */
1557  public void setInsertion(boolean insertion) {
1558    final boolean oldValue = this.insertion;
1559    this.insertion = insertion;
1560    if (this.insertion) // remove sorter before events for adding row
1561      checkCreateAddSorter(false);
1562    getModel().setInsertion(insertion);
1563    if (!this.insertion) // add sorter after events for removing rows
1564      checkCreateAddSorter(false);
1565    firePropertyChange("insertion", oldValue, this.insertion);
1566  }
